newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Manuel, Stals seen discussing fx control at weekend.
newsitem.headline: Manuel, Stals seen discussing fx control at weekend.

text.p: Finance Minister Trevor Manuel and Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals are likely to discuss details of the next steps in relaxing exchange controls at the weekend, a finance ministry spokeswoman said on Friday.
Manuel only arrived back in South Africa last night after a tour of Europe, Japan and the U.S., she added.
Markets are keenly awaiting details of the next phase in easing capital controls which will allow individuals to invest offshore for the first time from July 1.
The concession was announced in the March 12 budget, but details of the allowance are still awaited.
Both Stals and Manuel said during overseas visits last week that the offshore investment limit was likely to be set at around 160,000 rand -- equivalent to the travel allowance for a married couple.

Anxieties about the impact of capital outflows following July 1 have contributed to a weakening in the rand in recent weeks, although currency dealers said on Friday that some of the earlier concerns appeared to be abating.
News late on Thursday that the Reserve Bank had completed the first phase of talks on establishing a syndicated $1.5 billion medium-term credit facility helped assuage market fears.

The central bank said it was confident that any additional demands for foreign currency arising from the further relaxation of exchange controls, and not covered by a continued inflow of foreign capital, would be met.
